answer: A farm running 38 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the nadir stake is held until the basalt settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the wharf audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 26% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
